problem:
Which of the following statements are true given that $T:{R}^{7}\to {R}^{7}$ is a linear transformation whose standard matrix is $T,$ and $T({v}_{1})=T({v}_{2})$ for some distinct vectors  ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}?$ 

- $\text{Ker}(T)\ne {0}$
- $T$ is invertible
- $\text{rank}(T)=7$
worked_solution:
Since $T$ is a linear transformation from ${R}^{7}$ into ${R}^{7},$ the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

 $T$ is a bijection (an invertible transformation) $\,⟺\,{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Im}(T)={R}^{7} \\  & \text{rank}(T)=7 \\  & \text{Ker}(T)={0} \\  & \text{nullity}(T)=0\end{aligned}$ 

Since $T$ is a linear transformation, we have that

$$
T({v}_{1})=T({v}_{2})\,⟹\,T({v}_{1}-{v}_{2})=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true. Indeed, since ${v}_{1}-{v}_{2}\in \text{Ker}(T)$ and ${v}_{1}\ne {v}_{2},$ we must have that $\text{Ker}(T)\ne {0}.$

- Statement II is false. According to the invertible matrix theorem, since $\text{Ker}(T)\ne {0},$ the transformation $T$ and the matrix $T$ are not invertible.

- Statement III is false. Since $T$ is not invertible, the invertible matrix theorem implies that $\text{rank}(T)\ne 7.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
